title: LLM weight boarding bridge and consensus validation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Build a lightweight, production-safe "weight boarding bridge" that centralizes intake of community/open-source model weights, runs deterministic conversion paths, and produces a consensus-based validation profile used to recommend a pin and publish a performance profile. The bridge should be staged so that a fast smoke validates basic compatibility and an asynchronous full-profile pipeline computes throughput/latency/cost and quality signals. The goal is to reduce noisy manual review and enable safe auto-pinning for low-risk models while surfacing clear failure signals for human triage.

Out of scope: full safety/safety-signature workflows (handled by safety pipeline teams), advanced quantization heuristics (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Weight boarding API accepts a signed manifest and stores artifact metadata in the intake catalog (manifest and metadata schema validated).
Deterministic conversion run completes for a submitted weight and produces a canonical runtime artifact (converted weights + DAG of conversion steps).
Quick-smoke validation runs in < 15 minutes for 95% of submissions: shape checks, KV-cache exercise, basic generation sanity across 10 synthetic prompts.
Consensus validation step runs across at least two conversion backends and computes divergence metrics; if divergence > 0.03 token-level JS divergence, model is flagged for manual review.
Full-profile pipeline (async) publishes throughput/latency/cost/kv-cache-hit metrics and a recommended pin (model version + quantization profile) to the profile catalog UI.
Telemetry: per-model validation results, failure reasons, and conversion logs are available in Console under Models -> Onboarding for 90d retention.
Feature-flagged rollout with a canary set of ~20 community models and automated rollback if canary error rate > 5% for 24h.
implementation_notes: Architecture: intake API -> storage (s3 + manifest DB) -> conversion worker pool (isolated containers) -> smoke validator -> async profiler/benchmark runner -> profile publisher.

Consensus validation: run same model through converter A and converter B (TransformerConverter v2 and OrbitConverter v1) and compare token-level distributions using JS divergence on logits and BLEU/ROUGE for deterministic sequences.
Staging strategy: quick-smoke (blocking) then full-profile (async). Quick-smoke must be sufficient to detect major failures so we avoid wasted compute on full profiles for broken weights.

Failure policy: smoke failure = reject ingestion and notify uploader + create manual review task. Consensus divergence between converters = hold and create human review ticket with diff artifacts and sample generations.

Cost trade-offs: full profiling uses heterogeneous configurations (fp16/fp32/quantized) across representative GPUs — we run this only asynchronously to avoid inflating intake latency and cost. Pin recommendation is provisional until full-profile completes unless quick-smoke + heuristics indicate low risk.
Observability: add structured logs and spans for each stage (intake, conversion, smoke, consensus, profile). Expose counters for conversion time, smoke pass rate, divergence score distribution.
Security: manifests must be signed and validated; conversion runs in ephemeral VMs with process-level isolation. KMS keys used for any private artifacts.

2025-02-13 Security (R. Kaur): Asked for KMS usage for any customer-supplied keys. Confirmed manifest-only flows stay encrypted at rest; conversion VMs will not persist keys. Marked security_review_required = true.

2025-02-14 Design (Sofia Li): Suggested Console UI states for 'boarding: smoke passed / consensus flagged / profiling in progress'. Worked with UX to reserve an onboarding row in Models table. Design spec: https://drive.google.com/designs/boarding-ui

2025-02-16 Miguel Ramos: Implemented quick-smoke harness. Ran local smoke suite against 12 community models; 2 failed due to tokenizer mismatches (added tokenizer-normalizer to smoke). Test run metadata: run_id=smoke-20250216-07, logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/runs/smoke-20250216-07

2025-02-18 Asha Patel: Consensus algorithm tuned. Set provisional token divergence threshold = 0.03 based on baseline of 40 models. Adding note: threshold may be adjusted after canary results. Created canary plan doc in Confluence.
next_steps: Finish conversion shim for non-standard checkpoints (blocking, estimated 1d).
Wire up intake API to manifest DB and object store (s3) and add signed-manifest verification.
Deploy quick-smoke to the staging cluster behind FF and kick off canary run with 20 selected models.
After canary: gather metrics and decide threshold adjustments; enable provisional auto-pin for low-risk models.
